title: Cofinal base change for filtered infinity categories
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the filteredness convention of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Let $\kappa$ be an infinite regular cardinal. For a functor $u:I\to J$ between filtered infinity categories, call $u$ weakly cofinal when every $j\in J$ admits a morphism $j\to u(i)$ for some $i\in I$. Call $u$ $\kappa$-cofinal when, for every diagram $d:K\to I$ with $K$ $\kappa$-small and weakly contractible, the induced functor on cocone categories $I_{d/}\to J_{ud/}$ is weakly cofinal. Here $\kappa$-small means fewer than $\kappa$ nondegenerate simplices, weakly contractible means that the space obtained by inverting all arrows is contractible, and $I_{d/}$ consists of cocones under $d$.

Let $\kappa<\tau$ be infinite regular cardinals. Let $I\xrightarrow{u}J\xleftarrow{v}I'$ be functors between $\tau$-filtered infinity categories which admit colimits of all $\tau$-small $\kappa$-filtered diagrams. Suppose $u,v$ preserve these colimits and are $\kappa$-cofinal. Here the homotopy pullback consists of triples $(i,i',e:u(i)\simeq v(i'))$, with coherent commuting pairs of arrows and all their higher compatibilities. Then $I\times^h_J I'$ is $\tau$-filtered and both projections are $\kappa$-cofinal.

Every $\kappa$-cofinal functor between filtered infinity categories is cofinal: for any small such indexing categories and any diagram $H:J\to\mathcal E$, restriction along $u:I\to J$ identifies the colimit cocones of $H$ with those of $Hu$. In particular, an existing colimit of $H$ is also the colimit of its restriction, with the same cocone vertex.

source.place: Definition 5.4.5.8, Lemma 5.4.5.12, Lemma 5.4.6.5 and Proposition 4.1.1.8 Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Put $P=I\times^h_J I'$ and let $d:K\to P$ be any $\tau$-small diagram. Its projections give $d_I,d_{I'}$ and an equivalence $u d_I\simeq v d_{I'}$; write $d_J=u d_I$ and use this equivalence on the other leg. Set $A=I_{d_I/}$, $B=I'_{d_{I'}/}$ and $C=J_{d_J/}$, with induced maps $g:A\to C$, $h:B\to C$. The coherent triple model of [lem-coef-accessible-pullback-filtered-colimit] gives $P_{d/}\simeq A\times^h_C B$. Indeed a cocone on $d$ consists of one cocone in each component, an equivalence of their image vertices, and a coherent identification of the two induced $J$-cocones extending the equivalence already in $d$. A morphism is a pair of vertex arrows with precisely the commuting triangles of those two cocones. For every higher simplex the condition is the same compatibility on that simplex, so this identification retains all coherences and respects the two vertex projections. By [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-coslice-calculus], $A,B,C$ are $\tau$-filtered, admit all $\tau$-small $\kappa$-filtered colimits with vertices computed in $I,I',J$, and $g,h$ preserve these colimits and are $\kappa$-cofinal.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.6.5, first pullback diagram; Lemmas 5.3.1.21, 5.4.5.14 and 5.4.6.4

proof.text: Since $\kappa<\tau$, a $\kappa$-small shape is $\tau$-small; hence the $\tau$-filtered categories $A,B,C$ of step 1 are $\kappa$-filtered. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-common-image] to $g,h$. It supplies $a\in A$, $b\in B$ and an equivalence $g(a)\simeq h(b)$ in $C$. This is a vertex of $A\times^h_C B$, and therefore a cocone on $d$ in $P$. This works for every $\tau$-small $K$, including $K=\varnothing$, so $P$ is $\tau$-filtered. Only the auxiliary $\kappa$-filtered colimits used by the cited common-image lemma are taken; no colimit of the original arbitrary shape $K$ is assumed.

To prove $P\to I$ $\kappa$-cofinal, fix a $\kappa$-small weakly contractible $d:K\to P$ and any $a\in A=I_{d_I/}$. Retain $B,C,g,h$ from step 1 and put $c=g(a)$. Consider $A_a=A_{a/}$, $C_c=C_{c/}$ and $B_c=B\times^h_C C_c$. The first maps $A_a\to C_c$ and $B_c\to C_c$ are $\kappa$-cofinal, and these three categories are $\tau$-filtered, by the absolute and relative clauses of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-coslice-calculus] applied to $g,h$ and the one-point diagrams $a,c$. These clauses and [lem-coef-accessible-pullback-filtered-colimit] also give the needed $\tau$-small $\kappa$-filtered colimits and preservation: $A_a,C_c$ compute them at vertices; $B_c$ computes them in its two components, since $h$ and $C_c\to C$ preserve them; the projection $B_c\to C_c$ therefore preserves them. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-common-image] to these two maps. The resulting objects have the form $(a\to a_1)$ and $(b,c\to h(b))$, and their images are equivalent in $C_c$. In particular there is an equivalence $g(a_1)\simeq h(b)$ compatible with the arrows out of $c$. Thus $(a_1,b,e)$ gives a vertex $t\in P_{d/}$ and the arrow $a\to a_1$ is a morphism $a\to\operatorname{pr}_I(t)$ in $A$. This is exactly weak cofinality of $P_{d/}\to I_{d_I/}$, for each required $d$.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.6.5, proof for q-prime; Lemmas 5.4.6.4, 5.4.5.11 and 5.4.6.3

proof.text: For $P\to I'$, fix the same type of test diagram $d$ and a vertex $b\in B=I'_{d_{I'}/}$. Put $c=h(b)$, $B_b=B_{b/}$, $C_c=C_{c/}$ and $A_c=A\times^h_C C_c$. By [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-coslice-calculus], the functors $B_b\to C_c$ and $A_c\to C_c$ are $\kappa$-cofinal and their source and target categories are $\tau$-filtered. The vertex colimit clause gives the $\tau$-small $\kappa$-filtered colimits of $B_b,C_c$ and preservation for $B_b\to C_c$. In $A_c$ the colimits are componentwise by [lem-coef-accessible-pullback-filtered-colimit], because $g$ and $C_c\to C$ preserve them, so $A_c\to C_c$ preserves them too. The common-image lemma [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-common-image] supplies $(b\to b_1)$ in $B_b$ and $(a,c\to g(a))$ in $A_c$ with equivalent images in $C_c$. Inverting the resulting equivalence of target vertices gives $g(a)\simeq h(b_1)$, with its coherent compatibility under $c$. The triple $(a,b_1,e)$ is a vertex $t\in P_{d/}$, and $b\to b_1$ is an arrow $b\to\operatorname{pr}_{I'}(t)$ in $B$. This proves weak cofinality on the cocone category for every test diagram and hence $\kappa$-cofinality of the second projection.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.6.5, the second projection with its argument written out

proof.text: Finally let $f:D\to E$ be any $\kappa$-cofinal functor between filtered quasicategories, independent of the cospan above. For each $e\in E$, apply the relative clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-coslice-calculus] with filteredness cardinal $\tau=\aleph_0$ and the one-point diagram $\Delta^0\to E$ with value $e$. That shape is both $\kappa$-small and $\aleph_0$-small. The relative category $D_{e/}=D\times^h_E E_{e/}$ is therefore filtered, and is weakly contractible by [lem-coef-infinity-coslice-colimit-formula] with filteredness cardinal $\aleph_0$. For small $D,E$, [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-comma-criterion] now applies: restriction itself is an equivalence of coherent cocone categories over any target quasicategory, and on the spaces of cocones at each fixed vertex. It preserves and reflects the property of a given cocone being colimiting. This proves the final assertion, including its existing-colimit and unchanged-vertex clause; applying it to the two projections already proved $\kappa$-cofinal gives their ordinary cofinality as well.
